data.best_text: June to August for bright nights and open roads, September to March for the northern lights.
data.day_budget_note: Per person per day excluding flights: a share of a mid-range double room, food, local transport and one sight. A rough estimate.

stay.label: Weekend
stay.text: The city, the Blue Lagoon and the Golden Circle with Þingvellir, Strokkur and Gullfoss.

stay.label: Five days
stay.text: Time for the south coast with an overnight stop on the way.

stay.label: One week
stay.text: Add Vatnajökull or drive further east with a rental car.

areas.name: City centre (101)
areas.text: Walking distance to Hallgrímskirkja, Harpa and the restaurants. The most expensive area.

areas.name: Laugardalur
areas.text: Cheaper, close to the city's large outdoor pool. Bus into the centre.

transport.text: 45 minutes to the BSÍ bus terminal. A bus leaves 35–45 minutes after every arrival.

events.name: Dark Music Days
events.text: A festival for new and experimental music.

events.name: Winter Lights Festival
events.text: A light trail, museum night and pool night across the capital area. Free.

seasons.name: Puffins
seasons.text: They arrive in mid-April and leave in mid-August. Best from May to July.

seasons.name: Midnight sun
seasons.text: From mid-May to the end of July.

seasons.name: Whale watching
seasons.text: Runs all year, but the chances are best now. Best in June.

seasons.name: Highland roads open
seasons.text: From mid-June to early September. Four-wheel drive required.

seasons.name: Ice caves
seasons.text: Sources give different start dates, from October or November.

month_notes: Dark and cold. Season for northern lights and ice caves.
Winter with a little more light. Northern lights and ice caves.
The last good month for northern lights and ice caves.
Between seasons. The first puffins arrive in the middle of the month.
The puffins are in place and the midnight sun begins. Cool, and the highlands are closed.
Midnight sun, puffins and the best time for whale watching. The highland roads open in the middle of the month.
Warmest and most tourists. Puffins and open highlands. Book accommodation early.
The puffins leave in the middle of the month. Still summer, and the darkness returns.
Autumn colours, fewer tourists and the northern lights are back. The highland roads close at the start of the month.
Darker and wetter. Northern lights, and the ice caves begin to open.
Winter and short days. Northern lights and ice caves.
The darkest time of the year. Christmas lights, northern lights and ice caves.

prices.summary: Among Europe's most expensive cities, above all for food and alcohol.

rows.note: With drinks. The source's own pages give different amounts, hence only a range.

IS-fakta-inresa.title: Passport or national ID card
IS-fakta-inresa.summary: Bring a passport or national ID card. A driving licence does not normally count as a travel document.
IS-fakta-inresa.body: A national ID card is valid for travel within the EU and Schengen, which also includes Iceland and Norway. Within the Nordics a Swedish driving licence can be enough in some cases, but a passport or national ID card is recommended.

IS-fakta-mobil.title: Use data and call as at home
IS-fakta-mobil.summary: The same price as in Sweden for calls, texts and data.
IS-fakta-mobil.body: Roam-like-at-home also applies in the EEA countries Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway. Check whether your plan has a cap on data abroad.

IS-fakta-betala.title: Currency: Icelandic króna (ISK)
IS-fakta-betala.summary: The country uses the Icelandic króna (ISK).

IS-fakta-alkohol.title: Alcohol from age 20
IS-fakta-alkohol.summary: The age limit is 20 for all alcohol.
IS-fakta-alkohol.body: The state-run Vínbúðin has a monopoly on alcohol above 2.25 per cent. ID is checked both in shops and in bars.

IS-reykjavik-fakta-ta-sig-dit.title: Keflavik to Reykjavik in 45 minutes
IS-reykjavik-fakta-ta-sig-dit.summary: Flybus runs to BSÍ after every arriving flight.
IS-reykjavik-fakta-ta-sig-dit.body: The bus matches all arrivals, so you can take the one that is waiting. Wifi is available on board.

IS-fakta-surtsey.title: The island born from the sea
IS-fakta-surtsey.summary: The volcanic island of Surtsey has been a World Heritage Site since 2008.
IS-fakta-surtsey.body: Iceland has three World Heritage Sites: Þingvellir (2004), Surtsey (2008) and Vatnajökull (2019).

IS-thingvellir.name: Þingvellir
IS-thingvellir.summary: National park and World Heritage Site since 2004.
IS-thingvellir.body: The Althing was founded here in the year 930. The landscape and Lake Þingvallavatn belong together geologically.

IS-vatnajokull.name: Vatnajökull National Park
IS-vatnajokull.summary: Covers 14 per cent of Iceland, a World Heritage Site since 2019.
IS-vatnajokull.body: Volcanoes, glaciers and desert in the same park.

IS-reykjavik-hallgrimskirkja.name: Hallgrímskirkja
IS-reykjavik-hallgrimskirkja.summary: The church is free, the tower costs money.
IS-reykjavik-hallgrimskirkja.body: The city's landmark with a view from the tower. The church is used for services and concerts, so the tower and church may close temporarily.

IS-bla-lagunen.name: The Blue Lagoon
IS-bla-lagunen.summary: Must be booked in advance. The ticket has an arrival hour.
IS-bla-lagunen.body: The lagoon is usually fully booked all year. A ticket for 1 pm is valid for arrival between 1 and 2 pm, and then you can stay as long as you like. Everyone showers without swimwear before bathing.

IS-reykjavik-harpa.name: Harpa
IS-reykjavik-harpa.summary: The glass concert hall by the harbour. Free to enter.
IS-reykjavik-harpa.body: The public areas are open Sun–Tue 10 am–6 pm and Wed–Sat 10 am–8 pm. Concerts and guided tours require a ticket.

IS-strokkur.name: Strokkur and Geysir
IS-strokkur.summary: The geyser Strokkur erupts every six to ten minutes.
IS-strokkur.body: No entrance fee, free parking and always open. Located in Haukadalur, about 1.5 hours from Reykjavik. Geysir itself has been dormant since 2003.

IS-gullfoss.name: Gullfoss
IS-gullfoss.summary: The waterfall ten minutes east of Geysir.
IS-gullfoss.body: The third stop on the Golden Circle together with Þingvellir and Geysir.

mat-skyr.name: Skyr
mat-skyr.hint: A thick cultured dairy product eaten with a spoon.

daggdjur-islandshast.name: Icelandic horse
daggdjur-islandshast.hint: Small and shaggy, often standing by the roadside.

fagel-lunnefagel.name: Puffin
fagel-lunnefagel.hint: Black and white with a colourful beak, on the coast in summer.

naturfenomen-gejser.name: Erupting geyser
naturfenomen-gejser.hint: A hot spring that throws up water at regular intervals.

IS-reykjavik-ide-thingvellir.title: Day trip to Þingvellir
IS-reykjavik-ide-thingvellir.body: Walk in the rift valley where the Althing met.

IS-reykjavik-ide-kyrktornet.title: View from Hallgrímskirkja
IS-reykjavik-ide-kyrktornet.body: Go up the tower on a clear day and then walk down the main street.

IS-ide-bla-lagunen.title: The Blue Lagoon on the way to or from your flight
IS-ide-bla-lagunen.body: Book the time well in advance and put the bath on the first or last day.

IS-reykjavik-ide-gyllene-cirkeln.title: The Golden Circle
IS-reykjavik-ide-gyllene-cirkeln.body: Þingvellir, Strokkur and Gullfoss in one day. Works with a rental car or a bus tour.

IS-reykjavik-ide-harpa.title: Harpa at dusk
IS-reykjavik-ide-harpa.body: Go in and look at the glass façade from the inside, and continue along the harbour.

IS-present-ull.name: Icelandic wool
IS-present-ull.body: A hat or mittens are cheaper and lighter than a whole jumper.

IS-present-brennivin.name: Brennivín
IS-present-brennivin.body: Icelandic caraway spirit in a small bottle.

IS-present-mugg.name: Lava ceramic mug
IS-present-mugg.body: Local ceramics with a black, rough surface.
